issues.description: The problem statement's Part 2 describes a milk method with a double parameter (messageOnMilk(double milkVolume)), but the UML, template usage, and solution use a parameterless method (messageOnMilk()). This mismatch in the method signature for Milkable.messageOnMilk can confuse students about the required interface and prevents implementing a solution that matches all artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification, template, and solution. Either (A) update the problem statement to require a parameterless messageOnMilk() returning a String (matching the UML, template usage, and solution), and adjust the textual example to e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"; or (B) change the UML, template usages, and solution to define Milkable.messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update all call sites and implementations to accept the double parameter and format the return string with the volume. Option A is the simpler fix to preserve existing template/solution code.

issues.description: The problem statement's textual requirements specify a milk method signature messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and require the returned string to include the milk volume, but the UML and all code artifacts (template and solution) declare and use a no-argument messageOnMilk() that returns a string without volume. This mismatch (method signature and expected output) creates confusion about the correct API students must implement and test against.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification and implementation. Either (A) update the problem text to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and describe the simpler return (e.g., "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), or (B) update the UML, template, and solution to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and adjust all implementations and call sites (e.g., Main and tests) to pass a volume and include the volume in the returned string. Aligning the method signature and expected return across problem, template, and solution will remove student confusion.
